name: Hack Canada
description: A student hackathon bringing together hackers from universities across Canada, with travel reimbursement and over $10K in prizes. Free to attend for high school and university students. The 2026 edition was held in Waterloo; 2027 moves to the University of Toronto.

name: Hackfest CTF
description: 24-hour on-site capture-the-flag competition run during Hackfest, Canada's largest bilingual hacking and cybersecurity event; requires a Hackfest ticket plus a CTF ticket.

name: Capital Hacks
description: Three-day student hackathon at Sacramento State (formerly Hornet Hacks) run by the Carlsen Center for Innovation & Entrepreneurship and ACM Sac State, with civic/govtech, health, sustainability and wildcard tracks and $3,500 in cash prizes.

name: SIGCSE TS
audience: computer science educators, researchers, graduate students
description: ACM SIGCSE Technical Symposium, the largest computing-education conference: papers, panels, posters, Nifty Assignments, demos and an exhibit hall for CS educators.

name: California Government Technology Summit
audience: state and local government IT leaders, public-sector technologists, industry partners
description: One-day Government Technology summit for California state and local government on AI, cybersecurity, data governance and digital service delivery, with the State CIO among the keynotes.

name: MadHacks
description: UW-Madison's long-running 24-hour student hackathon, one of the largest in the Midwest, with mentorship, workshops, meals and prizes.

name: Israel Tech Week
description: Five-day programme in Miami connecting Israeli startups with U.S. investors and corporates: sector days on defense, cybersecurity, AI, fintech and healthtech, a startup showcase and a VC and investors summit.

name: HackMiami
description: South Florida's hacker conference: four days of paid security trainings followed by a two-track talks day.

name: Venture Madness
audience: tech founders, accredited investors, venture capital and private equity firms
description: One-day conference and expo where Arizona's most promising tech startups pitch to investors, run by Invest Southwest since 1992.

name: Venture Café Phoenix Thursday Gathering
description: Free weekly Thursday-evening gathering at the Phoenix Bioscience Core with mentor hours, workshops and talks on startups, AI and innovation, followed by networking.

name: Calgary Innovation Week
venue: Platform Innovation Centre (HQ) and venues across Calgary
audience: founders, investors, tech workers, students, community
description: Calgary's city-wide week of tech, innovation and entrepreneurship events, run by Platform Calgary with main-stage sessions at the Platform Innovation Centre and community-hosted offsite events; most sessions are free via its Luma calendar and the week closes with Calgary Launch Party.

name: Calgary Launch Party
description: Calgary's annual startup showcase since 2010, where the year's Top 10 early-stage Calgary startups, chosen by community nomination and expert review, demo their products on the closing night of Calgary Innovation Week.

name: Future Summit
description: One-day innovation summit in Calgary convening investors, entrepreneurs, government and industry leaders on the future of technology, AI and infrastructure.

name: CyberSci Calgary Regional
description: Calgary regional of Canada's Cyber Security Challenge: a one-day in-person capture-the-flag for post-secondary student teams, with sponsor interviews in the afternoon; winners advance to the National Finals in Ottawa.

name: Global Game Jam YYC
audience: game developers, artists, musicians, students, beginners
description: The Calgary Game Developers Association's in-person Global Game Jam site: a beginner-friendly weekend making games with meals, judges, prizes and a public playtest showcase.

name: Global Entrepreneurship Week Kansas City
audience: entrepreneurs, founders, small business owners, investors, students
description: Kansas City's Global Entrepreneurship Week at Union Station, run by KCSourceLink: expert-led sessions, speakers, a maker fair, an ecosystem-builder day and youth programming for founders at every stage.

name: Pipeline Innovators Pitch Showcase
venue: Union Station Planetarium, 30 W Pershing Road
description: Pipeline Entrepreneurs' annual pitch day, where the year's Fellows and Pathfinders, high-growth founders from across the Midwest, pitch to a national judging panel, followed in the evening by the Innovators Gala.

name: Waterloo Tech Week
description: A decentralized week of independently hosted talks, demos, panels, meetups and pitch events celebrating Waterloo's tech community, organised by the Hack the North team in the run-up to the hackathon.

name: Velocity Pitch Competition
venue: Science Teaching Complex, University of Waterloo
audience: University of Waterloo student founders, investors, community
description: Velocity's pitch competition for University of Waterloo student-led startups, running since 2011; the 2026 edition put teams through two-minute, no-slide pitches before 100 judges for a $5,000 top prize.

name: Impact Venture Demo Day
venue: Davidson Winter Garden, Ross School of Business
description: University of Michigan-wide demo day where 25+ student ventures from the Ross Impact Studio and partner programs show live prototypes in tech for good, health, education, climate and fintech to investors and the public.

name: MidwestCon
venue: 1819 Innovation Hub and venues across Cincinnati
description: Four-day AI and technology conference week in Cincinnati, centred on UC's 1819 Innovation Hub, combining policy and AI sessions, a hackathon, an art-and-AI showcase and partner events.

name: Capture Ohio: OCRI Statewide CTF
venue: Clifton Court Hall, University of Cincinnati
description: The Ohio Cyber Range Institute's annual one-day statewide capture-the-flag for student teams of three to five, hosted in person at the University of Cincinnati with partner campuses across Ohio joining the same day.

name: Ray Summit
audience: ML engineers, AI infrastructure and platform teams, researchers
description: Anyscale's three-day conference for the Ray open-source community: a hands-on training day followed by two days of keynotes and production talks on model training, multimodal data, RL and AI infrastructure, co-located with the vLLM Conference.

name: Commit Your Code
description: Community-built two-day developer conference in Dallas-Fort Worth from Dallas Software Developers: six technical tracks, Day 0 community events and a free livestream, with a $40 in-person ticket and all net ticket revenue donated to charity.

name: Midwest Tech Conference
audience: developers and tech enthusiasts, students free
description: Volunteer-run one-day community tech conference in mid-Missouri with talks and workshops for enthusiasts to experts; $10 tickets and free for students.

name: MAIS Hacks
description: McGill Artificial Intelligence Society's annual fall 48-hour AI hackathon at McGill, with workshops, mentoring and networking with Montreal researchers and companies.

name: CGU Hacks
description: Two-day transdisciplinary hackathon run by CGU's AI for Humanity Lab and CISAT, with workshops, mentoring and tracks in AI, GeoAI, cybersecurity and UI/UX, focused on ethical, human-centred innovation.

name: CUSEC
audience: university and college software engineering and computer science students
description: Canada's longest-running student-led software engineering conference: three days of talks, hands-on workshops, a sponsor career fair and evening socials, with school delegations from across the country.

name: QCon AI New York
audience: senior software engineers, architects, engineering leaders running AI in production
description: Two-day practitioner conference from the QCon organisers on running AI systems in production: agents, evals, AI code review, token costs and guardrails, with talks from senior engineers at companies such as LinkedIn, Netflix and DoorDash.

name: DesignCon
audience: hardware, chip, board and system design engineers
description: Engineering conference and expo for chip, board and system design, covering signal and power integrity, high-speed interconnects and test, with a technical programme and an exhibit hall.

name: DeisHacks
description: Brandeis University's 48-hour social-good hackathon, where student teams from every major build prototypes for challenges set by local nonprofit partners.

name: Global Power Platform Bootcamp Calgary
audience: Power Platform makers, developers, business analysts, IT professionals
description: Free one-day community-run Calgary stop of the worldwide Global Power Platform Bootcamp, with hands-on sessions and labs on Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot and agents.

name: Socratica
audience: makers, engineers, founders, researchers, designers, students
description: Weekly Sunday-morning co-working session run by an open collective of makers, engineers, founders and artists: introductions, two focused work blocks on personal projects, then open demos. Runs in term-length seasons (Fall, Winter, Spring) with occasional weeknight and showcase events; RSVP on Wygo.

name: Health Wildcatters Pitch Day
audience: healthcare founders, investors, health-system leaders, mentors
description: Demo day closing the Health Wildcatters accelerator's annual ten-week cohort: every startup in the class pitches to investors and the DFW health-innovation community, followed by a networking reception.

name: AI Tinkerers Dallas-Fort Worth
venue: Kiln (Dallas; address sent to accepted attendees)
audience: AI engineers, technical founders, ML practitioners
description: Evening demo nights for people building with AI: short live demos with code, architecture deep dives and networking, held roughly every one to two months. Attendance is by application.

name: TexSAW
venue: UT Dallas, Engineering and Computer Science West (ECSW)
description: Texas Security Awareness Week: an annual UT Dallas capture-the-flag competition with an internationally ranked online CTF plus a multi-day in-person programme of hands-on security workshops on campus.

name: Hack Indy
description: Purdue University in Indianapolis's flagship student hackathon, run by the Purdue Computer Science Club: a weekend of overnight hacking, workshops and keynotes, judged by industry experts.

name: Venture Club of Indiana Innovation Showcase
audience: founders, angel and venture investors, Indiana startup community
description: Indiana's long-running annual startup pitch competition: nominated Indiana startups pitch on the main stage for three minutes each, alongside keynotes and investor panels.

name: STL Game Jam
venue: University of Missouri-St. Louis, Millennium Student Center
description: St. Louis's Global Game Jam site, run by the local game-dev community: 48 hours to build a game solo or in a team, with food, round-the-clock room access and a closing showcase.

name: Arch Grants Innovation Summit
audience: investors, corporate innovation leaders, Arch Grants portfolio founders
description: Arch Grants' deal-flow summit pairing its portfolio founders with investors and corporate partners through a full afternoon of curated, double opt-in one-on-one meetings.

name: UVic Hacks
description: University of Victoria student hackathon club running several themed one- and two-day hackathons each term (startup, healthcare, social-impact, creative coding), plus workshops, on campus.

name: Victoria International Privacy & Security Summit
audience: public-sector privacy, security and IT professionals, CISOs, policymakers
description: Long-running in-person summit on privacy, cybersecurity and AI governance for the public sector and regulated industries, with keynotes, panels and workshops.

name: Charlotte Fintech Week
audience: fintech and insurtech founders, investors, bankers, corporate innovators
description: A week of community-hosted fintech and insurtech events across Charlotte (panels, workshops, pitch events, happy hours), anchored by RevTech Labs' Fintech + Insurtech Generations conference.

name: PitchBreakfast
venue: Sparkhouse West (Do Greater Foundation), 2400 Greenland Avenue
audience: founders, angel investors, Charlotte startup community
description: Charlotte's monthly breakfast founder showcase, held on the second Wednesday: three startups each give a six-minute pitch, then take ten minutes of feedback from an investor panel and the audience, followed by networking.

name: Charlotte AI Summit
venue: Central Piedmont Community College, Parr Center
audience: business leaders, founders, educators, career changers
description: Free, full-day community summit on applying AI in healthcare, finance, entrepreneurship and the workforce, with speakers from regional employers and tech firms.

name: UnDemo Day
audience: Michigan startup founders, venture capital investors
description: Renaissance Venture Capital's annual day connecting Michigan startups with VCs from across the US through pre-matched 1:1 meetings, startup education and open networking; startups apply in advance for meeting tables.

name: Edmonton Startup Week
description: Edmonton Unlimited's annual week of startup events across the city: panels, lunch-and-learns, workshops and mentorship, the Startup Crawl and the Launch Party showcasing the year's top 10 startups.

name: Mission Accepted Space Hackathon
venue: Goldberg Computer Science Building, Dalhousie University, 6050 University Avenue
description: A weekend student hackathon at Dalhousie on space, satellite and Earth-observation data problems, mentored and judged by people from MDA Space and the Canadian Space Agency; runs at the start of Dal Innovation Week.

name: Global Game Jam Halifax
venue: ShiftKey Labs, Goldberg Computer Science Building, 6050 University Avenue
description: Halifax's in-person Global Game Jam site, hosted by ShiftKey Labs at Dalhousie: a non-competitive weekend making a game from scratch around the worldwide theme.

name: Dal Innovation Week
description: Dalhousie University's annual week of entrepreneurship and innovation events on campus, with pitch competitions, workshops, a space hackathon and Dal Demo Day, where accelerator and ideaHUB startups demo and pitch.

name: Upfront Summit
audience: LPs, venture capitalists, founders, corporate executives
description: Upfront Ventures' invitation-only annual gathering of LPs, VCs, founders and executives in Los Angeles, two days of talks and networking.

name: LA CTF
description: ACM Cyber at UCLA's annual capture-the-flag; the weekend competition is played online, with an in-person day at UCLA for talks, side events and team play. UCLA and Open divisions.

name: Twin Cities Startup Week
venue: Venues across Minneapolis and Saint Paul
description: Five days of startup programming across Minneapolis and Saint Paul, each day hosted at a different campus or venue, including the Startup World Cup Twin Cities regional pitch final and a community give-back hackathon.

name: Analytics for Good Hackathon
venue: Carlson School of Management, University of Minnesota
audience: University of Minnesota Twin Cities and Duluth students only
description: A two-day student analytics hackathon at Minnesota Carlson where teams work a mission-driven community organisation's data and business problem, mentored and judged by analytics professionals. Open to UMN students only.

name: UB Hacking
audience: university students from UB and nearby colleges
description: The University at Buffalo's student-run hackathon, running since 2012: a weekend of building, workshops and prizes billed as Western New York's largest hackathon.

name: Datathon PolyFinances
audience: university students in data science, engineering and finance
description: PolyFinances' weekend datathon at Polytechnique Montréal: teams of four solve a financial-analysis data challenge set by industry partners, followed by finalist pitches and a networking evening.

name: WiE Hackathon
venue: Pearl Sullivan Engineering Building (PSE), University of Waterloo
description: University of Waterloo Women in Engineering's one-day hackathon for women and non-binary students, with sponsor workshops, team matching and prizes.

name: Global Game Jam - Carleton University
description: Carleton University's Ottawa site for the Global Game Jam: a weekend jam in late January where teams build a game on the worldwide theme, held in person at Carleton with a Discord option for remote jammers.

name: Bioscience Association Manitoba AI Summit
audience: business leaders, bioscience and agri-food companies, AI practitioners
description: A one-day summit run by Bioscience Association Manitoba with partners, on how organisations in health, agriculture and clean tech are actually adopting AI, with panels, keynotes and networking.

name: RampUp Weekend
description: North Forge's 50-hour startup sprint in Winnipeg: participants pitch ideas, form teams and build an MVP over a weekend with mentor support, ending in final pitches.

name: Rhythm & Algorithm
audience: developers, designers, civic and nonprofit leaders, students
description: A two-day civic AI event at the New Orleans convention center: cross-sector teams prototype AI solutions to city challenges in a solutions sprint and pitch for prizes, alongside a one-day conference of panels and demos.

name: EXPLORE Pittsburgh Tech Week
audience: founders, corporate leaders, educators, students, job seekers
description: A citywide week of community-hosted tech events across Pittsburgh neighbourhoods: signature sessions, upskilling days, a startup pitch competition and a community calendar of meetups and workshops.

name: StartUP PGH
audience: founders, investors, researchers, students, corporate partners
description: A region-wide startup week where Pittsburgh's universities, accelerators and investors line up their flagship events, including CMU's Lab to Market and AI Robotics Venture Day and Innovation Works' Venture Expo.

name: Think!AI Summit
audience: AI practitioners, IT and business leaders, data teams
description: The Pittsburgh Technology Council's annual one-day AI summit (formerly Beyond Big Data), built around short tech talks from people deploying AI inside their organisations, from agentic workflows to physical AI and healthcare.

name: Pittsburgh Global Game Jam
venue: Sorrells Library, Wean Hall, Carnegie Mellon University
description: The Pittsburgh IGDA's Global Game Jam site at Carnegie Mellon: an online Friday kickoff, then a weekend of in-person jamming, playtesting and a Sunday showcase in Wean Hall.

name: Lassonde Demo Day
audience: student founders, investors, the Salt Lake startup community
description: The University of Utah Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute's end-of-year showcase where student startups demo their products, with attendees given 'Lassonde Dollars' to buy from the teams.

name: Utah Tech Week
description: A grassroots week of community-hosted events across Salt Lake City and Lehi, from pitch competitions and panels to dinners and parties, with opening and closing parties open to all.

name: San Diego Startup Week
venue: Multiple venues: Carlsbad, Carmel Valley, UC San Diego, Torrey Pines, SDSU
description: Startup San Diego's annual region-wide week of founder programming, now in its fourteenth year: five days at five venues from Carlsbad to SDSU, with panels, workshops, a founders showcase, expos and pitch competitions.

name: DataHacks
description: UC San Diego's 36-hour, in-person data science hackathon run by the Data Science Student Society, with mentoring, judging and prizes for student teams building with data and machine learning.

name: AI Tinkerers San Diego
venue: Rotating venues; Nov 17 meetup at 811 Prospect Street (La Jolla)
audience: AI engineers, technical founders, ML practitioners
description: Demo-first evening meetups for people building with AI: short code-first live demos with technical Q&A, then networking, held every one to three months. Attendance is by registration and screening.

name: H-Town Roundup
venue: Various locations across Houston, including the Ion
description: Houston Exponential's week-long celebration of Greater Houston's startup ecosystem, formerly Houston Tech Rodeo: dozens of talks, open houses, pitch events and receptions across the city's innovation hubs.

name: AI Tinkerers Houston
venue: Rotating venues; Nov 10 meetup at 2339 Commerce St
audience: AI engineers, technical founders, ML practitioners
description: Monthly evening meetups for people building with AI: vetted live demos of working systems, architecture discussion and networking. Attendance is by registration.

name: Oregon Startup Week
venue: Big Pink (U.S. Bancorp Tower) and venues across Portland
description: Oregon's statewide startup week, formerly Portland Startup Week: 40+ events over six days based at Big Pink in downtown Portland, with workshops, pitch sessions, demo days and founder networking.

name: Silicon Forest Tech Summit
description: A one-day Pacific Northwest tech summit run by STEAM Circuit: keynotes, industry and startup lightning talks, robot and product demos, and cross-industry networking for the Portland-area tech community.

name: GRO Demo Day
venue: Park Alumni Center, NC State, 2450 Alumni Dr
description: Demo day closing each cohort of CED's twelve-week GRO Incubator: graduating early-stage founders give five-minute pitches and compete for cash prizes, followed by networking.

name: Raleigh-Durham Startup Week
description: Five days of free workshops, keynotes, investor matching and networking across the Triangle, with 100+ sessions in Durham and Raleigh for startups at every stage.

name: AI Tinkerers Raleigh
venue: Rotating venues, e.g. Raleigh Founded (North Street), 1070 Partners Way
audience: AI engineers, technical founders, ML practitioners
description: In-person evening meetups for AI practitioners in the Triangle: live demos of working AI systems, hands-on sessions and networking, held every two to three months.

name: VandyHacks
description: Vanderbilt's official collegiate hackathon, running since 2015: a weekend of in-person building with workshops, speakers, games, meals and sponsor challenges, open to students of every experience level.

name: Nashville Entrepreneur Day
description: The Nashville Entrepreneur Center's twice-yearly demo day, where its TakeOff, InFlight and Project Healthcare accelerator cohorts graduate: a founder expo plus two pitch tracks competing for non-dilutive grants awarded on stage.

name: AI Tinkerers Nashville
venue: Rotating venues; Nov 17 meetup at 5501 Virginia Way #120, Brentwood
audience: AI engineers, technical founders, ML practitioners
description: Builders' meetups for people working hands-on with AI in Middle Tennessee: live demos, code and architecture walkthroughs and networking, roughly every two months.

name: Merge
description: SoftwareGR's annual West Michigan software conference where product managers, designers and developers meet; the 2026 theme was AI at Work.

name: Into The Box
description: Ortus Solutions' annual conference for the ColdBox, BoxLang and CFML community: a pre-conference workshop day followed by two days of sessions on modern web development.

name: Agent Conference
description: Two-day enterprise conference on autonomous AI agents, programmed in ten themes from engineering and security to finance and healthcare.

name: Canadian Women in Cybersecurity
audience: women in cybersecurity, security leaders and practitioners
description: siberX's one-day Toronto conference celebrating and advancing women in Canadian cybersecurity, with talks, panels and networking.

name: MLSys
description: The annual academic Conference on Machine Learning and Systems: research papers, keynotes and an industry track on training, inference and ML infrastructure.

name: UXDX New York
description: Cross-functional conference where product, research, design and engineering teams learn together through talks and workshops.

name: Data Summit
audience: data leaders, architects, engineers, analytics teams
description: DBTA's annual data management, analytics and AI conference in Boston, with workshops, a Data + AI Leadership Forum and a solutions showcase.

name: GDGHacks
description: Free in-person student hackathon run by Google Developer Groups at the University of Guelph, drawing hackers from dozens of universities.

name: DesignVerse
audience: undergraduate, graduate and high school students
description: UC Riverside's 24-hour beginner-friendly design-a-thon: teams design an app or website interface to a prompt and present it to industry judges.

name: Miami Startup Ecosystem Conference
description: Two-day Miami conference of fireside chats, workshops and startup demo tables for founders and active investors, run by Denis Hiller and 1001 VC.

name: AI DevSummit
audience: AI developers, engineering managers, AI executives
description: DevNetwork's conference and expo for AI developers and leaders, with tracks on models, data, AI ops and strategy, plus a hackathon and startup alley.

name: Open Source North
description: Minnesota's one-day open source and enterprise software conference, now in its twelfth year, with talks from Twin Cities practitioners and a sponsor hall.

name: QCon AI Boston
audience: senior software engineers, architects, engineering leaders running AI in production
description: Two-day practitioner conference from the InfoQ/QCon organisers on running AI in production, successor to the InfoQ Dev Summit Boston.

name: Day of Data
description: Free one-day community data conference from Utah Geek Events, formerly SQL Saturday Salt Lake City, with four tracks on SQL Server, PostgreSQL and other database platforms.

name: DevRelCon New York
audience: developer relations, developer experience and developer marketing professionals
description: Two-day conference for developer relations, DevX and developer marketing practitioners, run by MLH, with a mini hackathon the night before.

name: ETHDenver
description: Community-run Ethereum festival in Denver, held since 2018, combining a conference with the BUIDLathon hackathon. The 2027 tenth edition is a two-day event.

name: Wild West Hackin' Fest @ Mile High
description: Black Hills Information Security's Denver edition of Wild West Hackin' Fest: technical talks, hands-on labs, villages and a CTF, preceded by two days of Antisyphon pre-conference training.

name: Colorado Game Jam
venue: Roser ATLAS Building, University of Colorado Boulder
description: In-person weekend game jam run by CU Game Dev at CU Boulder. The theme is revealed at kickoff, teams get three days to build, mentors are on hand, and there are cash prizes. Generative AI is banned.

name: DU Arcade
venue: Ritchie School of Engineering and Computer Science, University of Denver
description: Annual one-day student-organised game expo at the University of Denver, where student and local developers show playable games, with talks and panels on the games industry.

name: Tampa Bay Tech Week
audience: founders, tech professionals, executives, investors, students
description: Decentralised, region-wide technology week held across neighbourhoods in Tampa and St. Petersburg: keynotes, panels, workshops, startup showcases and community-hosted side events.

name: Orlando Game Jam
description: Orange County Library System's annual weekend game jam at the Melrose Center. It ends in a public Orlando Gaming Expo, where judges' scores and attendee votes decide the cash-prize winners.

name: Indie Galactic Space Jam
audience: game developers, artists, engineers, space-industry professionals
description: Indienomicon's 48-hour in-person game jam built around challenges from the space industry. Teams form on site and prototype games and simulations.

name: Global Game Jawn
audience: game developers, artists, students, first-time jammers
description: Philly Game Mechanics' Philadelphia site for the Global Game Jam: an in-person weekend jam at Indy Hall, with a week-long virtual track alongside.

name: Pennovation Accelerator Pitch Day
description: The pitch afternoon that closes Penn's six-week Pennovation Accelerator. The cohort of pre-seed and seed Philadelphia startups pitch to investors, mentors and the public.

name: Texas Game Jam
description: EGaDS!' annual weekend game jam at UT Austin, with an on-campus kickoff and industry mentors. It is open to anyone in Austin and can also be joined online.

name: BostonHacks
description: Boston University's annual 24-hour student hackathon, held in person at the George Sherman Union with workshops, panels and sponsor prizes; MLH member event.

name: HackBeanpot
description: An annual weekend hackathon for undergraduates run by a Boston-area non-profit, with beginner-friendly workshops, mentors and guest speakers.

name: Startup Boston Week
description: New England's largest annual startup gathering: five days of free sessions, panels and networking held across Boston University and Downtown Crossing each September.

name: Boston Globe Tech Innovation Summit
description: The Boston Globe's annual one-day summit of New England tech leaders, with panels on AI, climate tech, health tech and fintech and the release of the Tech Power Players 50 list.

name: Techstars Boston Demo Day
description: Closing showcase of the Techstars Boston accelerator cohort, where its startups (AI/ML, robotics, healthtech, tech bio) pitch to investors and the local ecosystem.

name: Boston Game Dev Global Game Jam
description: Boston Game Dev's in-person Global Game Jam site near South Station: a late-January weekend of team formation and game making on the worldwide theme, with industry mentors on hand.

name: Georgetown Ventures Demo Day
venue: Lohrfink Auditorium, Hariri Building, Georgetown University
description: Twice-yearly showcase closing Georgetown Ventures' 10-week student-run accelerator, where each cohort's founders pitch the progress they have made.

name: Global Game Jam - OSU Game Creation Club
description: Ohio State's Game Creation Club hosts a Global Game Jam site each January: a 48-hour jam in Sullivant Hall open to anyone 18+, with a Discord option.

name: Techstars Columbus Demo Day
description: Closing pitch event of the Techstars Columbus Powered by The Ohio State University accelerator, where the fall cohort presents to Columbus investors and mentors.

name: Global Game Jam - Georgia State University CMII
venue: Creative Media Industries Institute, 25 Park Place NE
description: Georgia State's Creative Media Industries Institute hosts a Global Game Jam site each January, with lab PCs, a keynote and a final showcase judged by Georgia Game Developers Association members.

name: CREATE-X Demo Day
audience: investors, founders, students, Atlanta innovation community
description: Georgia Tech's annual showcase of startups launched through the CREATE-X Startup Launch accelerator, where 100+ founding teams pitch and demo at booths.

name: Atlanta Tech Talks
venue: Manny's Tavern, 580 Woodward Ave SE (Grant Park)
audience: developers, engineers, data scientists, founders, students
description: A monthly evening of talks and hands-on workshops for Atlanta tech enthusiasts, held every third Thursday at a Grant Park tavern; running since 2011.

name: Uncommon Hacks
description: The University of Chicago's annual 24-hour student hackathon, held on campus each spring since 2019.

name: SparkHacks
description: A student-led 24-hour hackathon at the University of Illinois Chicago, run with UIC's Department of Computer Science, with workshops, mentors and track prizes.

name: Capture the Flame
venue: UIC Academic and Residential Complex, 940 W Harrison St
description: An annual one-day intercollegiate Capture the Flag competition at UIC for Chicagoland students, with beginner and advanced tracks in cryptography, forensics, reverse engineering and web security.

name: UChicago Deep Tech Demo Day
description: The Polsky Center's annual showcase of University of Chicago deep tech startups during TechChicago Week, with pitches in quantum and hardtech, healthcare, and data and AI, followed by a networking reception.

name: AI in Production
audience: product managers, software developers and teams building AI products
description: One-day, single-track conference in Asheville on practical strategies for building and deploying AI products, with lightning talks and birds-of-a-feather sessions.

name: SQL Saturday Baton Rouge
description: Free community day of data and IT training (now branded Day of Data) from the Baton Rouge User Groups, with preconference workshops the Friday before.

name: Agile2027
audience: agile practitioners, coaches, product and engineering leaders
description: Agile Alliance's annual conference, now run jointly with PMI; the host city changes each year.

name: Laracon US
description: The flagship US conference of the Laravel PHP framework, two days of talks and product announcements; it moves to a different US city each year.

name: Buffer-Free Video^AI
description: #BuffConf: a no-sales-pitch conference on production lessons in video streaming, media infrastructure and AI, hosted by Momento.

name: EUC World Amplify
audience: EUC architects and engineers, IT directors, virtualization administrators
description: Vendor-agnostic three-day conference of the World of EUC non-profit for end-user computing and virtualization professionals; the host city changes each year.

name: The Reinforcement Learning Conference (RLC)
description: Academic conference for reinforcement learning research, publishing in the Reinforcement Learning Journal; its location changes each year, and 2027 is split between Brown University and Odense.

name: AI Risk Summit
audience: security, risk and technology leaders, AI researchers, policy makers
description: SecurityWeek's in-person conference on securing AI in the enterprise, AI governance and adversarial AI, held alongside its CISO Forum Summer Summit.

name: Model-Based Systems Engineering in Practice
audience: systems engineers, acquisition professionals, MBSE practitioners
description: One-day conference from Carnegie Mellon's Software Engineering Institute on practical adoption of model-based systems engineering.

name: Outside LLMs
description: The official AI buildathon of the Outside Lands music festival; winning apps are demoed and shipped to festival-goers.

name: UHackathon
description: 24-hour student build sprint at UW Tacoma run by the Tech Startup Club, with production and experimental tracks and in-person demos.

name: CAST
audience: software testers, QA and quality engineering practitioners
description: The annual Conference of the Association for Software Testing, a practitioner-run conference on context-driven software testing; the host city changes each year.

name: HPE Nonstop Technology and Business Conference
description: The annual gathering of the HPE NonStop user community, run by Connect Worldwide: three days of technical sessions, HPE roadmap briefings and a vendor expo, with an HPE Education Day beforehand. The host city changes each year.

name: SquiggleConf
description: A single-track conference about developer tools (linters, editors, AI coding tools, debuggers) held in the New England Aquarium's IMAX theatre, with a launch party and a morning fun run.

name: InfoSec Nashville
description: The ISSA Middle Tennessee Chapter's annual security conference, running for 25 years: a day of hands-on workshops and a capture-the-flag, then a full conference day with keynotes, breakouts and an exhibit hall.

name: Enterprise AI Summit
description: IT Revolution's successor to the DevOps Enterprise / Enterprise Technology Leadership Summit, hosted by Gene Kim: experience reports from large organisations shipping AI and agent-written code in production. The host city changes with each edition.

name: API Conference New York
venue: New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge
description: A conference on API design, management, security and AI-era connectivity, run alongside DevOpsCon, MLcon and the JavaScript Conference as devmio's New York Week, with workshop days and an online option.

name: MLcon New York
venue: New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge
description: A machine learning and generative AI engineering conference with workshop days, part of devmio's New York Week alongside DevOpsCon, the JavaScript Conference and API Conference; in person in Brooklyn with an online option.

name: DYNA
description: Dyalog North America's free in-person user meeting for the APL community, with talks from Team Dyalog and APL users from across the Americas.

name: DevFest DC
description: GDG Washington DC's annual DevFest: a day of talks on AI agents, cloud and Google developer tools plus a companion build-a-thon, held at George Mason's Arlington campus.

name: SREday San Francisco
description: A one-day, two-track community conference on site reliability, DevOps, cloud and observability, held in San Francisco twice a year as part of the worldwide SREday series.

name: DubHacks
description: The Pacific Northwest's largest collegiate hackathon, a weekend of building run each October by UW students on the University of Washington campus.

name: DubHacks NEXT Demo Day
description: End-of-batch showcase for DubHacks NEXT, UW's student-run startup incubator, where the year's cohort of student startups pitch to investors and the community.

name: Global Game Jam - Seattle Interactive Media Lab (SiM)
venue: Seattle Interactive Media Lab, Northwest Worklofts, 3131 Western Ave Unit 421
description: A small community-run Global Game Jam site in Seattle, where teams build a game to the worldwide secret theme over one weekend in a creative co-working space.

name: Global Game Jam - Seattle Indies
venue: DigiPen Institute of Technology (also AIE Seattle)
description: Seattle Indies' annual Global Game Jam site and its biggest in-person jam: a 48-hour weekend at DigiPen in Redmond, with a second room at AIE in Seattle, ending in streamed presentations.

name: Global Game Jam - LaSalle College Vancouver
description: LaSalle College Vancouver's Global Game Jam site: a week of evening jam sessions open to the public, building games to the worldwide theme.

name: Global Game Jam Vancouver
description: Metro Vancouver's main Global Game Jam site since 2010: an in-person weekend at Douglas College where teams build a game from scratch, ending in an arcade showcase.

name: Gina Cody School Innovation Fund Demo Day
description: Concordia's Gina Cody School of Engineering and Computer Science showcase, where its funded student-led startups pitch for $20K judges' awards after a six-month programme.

name: AngelNV Finale
description: StartUpNV's annual live pitch finale, where Nevada startup finalists pitch a room of angel investors who decide on the spot who receives a $400K+ investment.

name: CyberWeek@UNLV Capture the Flag
description: A one-day in-person team CTF at UNLV during CyberWeek, covering cryptography, forensics, OSINT and reverse engineering, with mentors on hand for first-timers.

name: Tech Alley Vegas
description: Las Vegas's monthly 'meetup of meetups': a free all-day Saturday where up to 15 local tech, startup and investor groups run sessions under one roof.

name: Tech@NYU Startup Week
description: Tech@NYU's week of startup programming: a 48-hour Buildathon, founder and operator panels, company office tours and a closing social.

name: Techstars NYC Demo Day
description: Closing showcase of the Techstars New York City accelerator cohort, where its startups pitch to investors and the city's tech ecosystem.

name: University of Toronto Entrepreneurship Week
venue: Multiple venues across U of T's three campuses
description: U of T's annual week of public startup events across its three campuses: founder showcases, fireside chats and tri-campus pitch competitions, including the Desjardins Startup Prize with more than $100K in prizes. Each event is registered for separately.

name: CyberSci Toronto Regional
description: Toronto regional of Canada's Cyber Security Challenge: a one-day in-person capture-the-flag for post-secondary student teams, with sponsor interviews in the afternoon; winners advance to the National Finals in Ottawa.

name: The Jam @ GDC
description: The official two-day GDC game jam, run with Global Game Jam at the Moscone Center on the weekend GDC opens. About 100 jammers chosen by application get a GDC pass and show their jam games in the Festival Hall during the week.

name: UMassCTF
audience: students, CTF players of all skill levels
description: The UMass Cybersecurity Club's annual weekend jeopardy-style CTF (pwn, rev, web, forensics, OSINT) with prizes. Teams play online worldwide; the club runs an in-person opening ceremony and room on the UMass Amherst campus.

name: Innovation Challenge: The Final
description: The public final of UMass Amherst's flagship student startup competition, run by the Berthiaume Center: finalist teams pitch to alumni judges and a live audience for a $65,000 equity-free prize pool.

name: Voices of Data Science Conference
description: A student-run one-day data science conference at UMass Amherst's Manning CICS, with talks, panels and networking on a yearly theme; 2026 focused on agentic AI and autonomous systems.

name: UGA Venture Prize Competition
description: UGA Entrepreneurship's annual evening pitch competition in downtown Athens, where University of Georgia student founders pitch their startups for $17,500 in prizes before judges and a free public audience.

name: Cognite Impact
audience: industrial operations leaders, data and AI engineers
description: Cognite's flagship conference on industrial AI and data, with customer keynotes, breakout sessions and networking for the energy and manufacturing sectors.

name: LDX3 New York
audience: engineering managers, staff+ engineers, engineering executives
description: LeadDev's New York festival for engineering leadership, combining the former LeadDev, StaffPlus and LeadingEng New York conferences into two days of talks, workshops and an expo.

name: UXCON
audience: UX designers, researchers, product managers, engineers
description: Community UX conference run by UX University in downtown Silver Spring, near DC, bringing designers, researchers and product people together for talks, workshops and a happy hour.

name: MozCon
description: Moz's SEO and AI-search marketing conference, now run as a one-day, single-track in-person roadshow with a New York stop.

name: Kong Summit
audience: platform engineers, API and AI engineers, engineering leaders
description: Kong's annual API + AI summit with technical breakouts, hands-on labs, certification and an expo; the host city changes year to year and the 2027 location is not yet announced.

name: Current
description: Confluent's data streaming conference on Apache Kafka, Flink and Iceberg, with 80+ sessions, certification and an expo; the US edition moves between cities.

name: [un]prompted
audience: security practitioners, CISOs, AI security researchers
description: Practitioner-focused AI security conference with talks, demos and workshops covering offense, threat hunting and program building.

name: SREcon Americas
audience: site reliability engineers, systems and platform engineers
description: USENIX's three-day conference for engineers who run complex distributed systems at scale, covering site reliability, systems engineering and incident practice.

name: DAM Los Angeles
audience: digital asset management, content operations and martech professionals
description: Henry Stewart's West Coast digital asset management conference: two tracks and 60+ speakers on DAM systems, metadata and taxonomy, workflow integration and AI in content operations.

name: GW OSCON
audience: students, faculty, open source developers, OSPO staff
description: George Washington University's annual two-day open source conference, hosted by its Open Source Program Office, bringing together students, faculty and open source practitioners from the DC area.

name: Global AI Conference Toronto
audience: developers, engineers and researchers building AI agents
description: The Toronto stop of the Global AI Community's free one-day developer conference on building AI agents (formerly AgentCon), with live demos, deep dives and hands-on workshops run by the local chapter.

name: Data Saturday Chicago
audience: database administrators, data engineers, BI and analytics professionals
description: A volunteer-run community conference on the Microsoft Data Platform (database administration, cloud, BI, analytics and AI) with a pre-conference training day, from the team behind SQL Saturday Chicago.
